CoOccurrenceStat.description:
A technology that appears alongside this skill more often than its
base rate in the same scope predicts (lift >= the floor).
CoOccurrenceStat.title: CoOccurrenceStat

JobFilters.description: Everything is optional; the empty filter means the national market.
JobFilters.title: JobFilters

LoginRequest.description:
Login does not re-validate password length: complexity rules change
over time and must never lock an existing account out of signing in.
LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

MatchJobSummary.description:
Enough of a job to render and link a match card. Deliberately no
description: matches never serve posting text — the job-detail endpoint
does, under the display-policy gate.
MatchJobSummary.title: MatchJobSummary

MatchProfileSummary.description:
The candidate side of the match, for context and honesty: how many
skills actually join the taxonomy, which title families were matched
on, and the derived seniority the experience component used.
MatchProfileSummary.title: MatchProfileSummary

MatchWeights.description: The nominal component weights, surfaced so the ranking is legible.
MatchWeights.title: MatchWeights

MetaResponse.description: Everything the filter UI needs to render its options.
MetaResponse.title: MetaResponse

ProfileUpdate.description:
Full-document replacement. `reviewed` is the document state, not an
event: true sets reviewed_at (now, if not already set), false clears
it — editing after review naturally un-reviews by sending false.
ProfileUpdate.title: ProfileUpdate

RelaxationOption.description:
One honest way out of a zero-result search: what would change,
and how many jobs that buys. Never applied server-side.
RelaxationOption.title: RelaxationOption

SalaryOut.description:
Both representations, deliberately: raw for honest display
('$60/hr'), normalized annual USD for anything comparative.
SalaryOut.title: SalaryOut

SavedJobIdsResponse.description:
The ids the current user has saved — the search/detail UIs use this to
render the Save button's saved state without leaking anything else.
SavedJobIdsResponse.title: SavedJobIdsResponse

SavedJobMatch.description:
The M9 match for a saved job, minus the job (which the card already
holds). Present only when the user has a reviewed profile to match
against; `score` may be 0 for a saved job with no overlap — a saved job
is always explained, never dropped.
SavedJobMatch.title: SavedJobMatch

SearchFacets.description: Counts over the full matching set, not just the returned page.
SearchFacets.title: SearchFacets

SkillIn.description:
Keep an existing skill (id) or add a manual one (label, optionally
mapped to a taxonomy slug so it stays matchable).
SkillIn.title: SkillIn

SkillSalary.description:
Percentiles over disclosed-salary jobs with this skill, plus the
all-jobs national baseline the delta is measured against.
SkillSalary.title: SkillSalary

post.description:
Exchange email + password for a session cookie. A wrong email or
password is an indistinguishable 401 (no account-enumeration signal).

Revoke the current session and clear the cookie. Idempotent: safe to
call without a valid session (no error, cookie still cleared).

Create an account and sign the new user in (a session cookie is set),
so the client can move straight into resume onboarding.

get.description:
List matching active jobs with facet counts and keyset pagination.

Both the count and the rows come from the shared predicate — this is
the endpoint dashboard stats click through to, and its total must
always equal the number the user clicked.

get.description:
The current user's profiles only — the query is scoped to the
session, so it can never surface another account's data.

delete.description: Delete the profile and its uploaded resume (user-owned data).

put.description:
Full-document reconcile: id = keep/update, no id = create as
manual, absent = delete. One transaction — the review screen's Save.

get.description:
Rank active jobs against this profile (M9). The profile must belong to
the signed-in user (404 otherwise) and be reviewed (409 otherwise —
invariant #9: an unreviewed extraction is not usable). Accepts the same
`JobFilters` the market surface does; the candidate job pool is the
shared predicate, so the counts agree with search.

schema.title: Employment Type

post.description:
Rebuild the profile from the stored resume text, discarding all
edits — an explicit user action (ADR-005), useful after taxonomy
growth. The resume bytes and text are untouched.

Upload a PDF resume: parse, extract, and return the structured
profile in one synchronous call (the pipeline is deterministic rules,
well under a second). The resume and profile are owned by the uploading
user. Re-uploading identical bytes is idempotent and returns the user's
existing profile untouched — edits survive.

get.description:
The saved-jobs dashboard: each saved job with a live match score,
matched/missing skills, and reasons drawn from the user's most recently
reviewed profile.

post.description: Save a job. Idempotent; returns the updated saved-id set.

get.description:
The ids the user has saved — for rendering the Save button's state in
search and job detail. Saved jobs stay in search; this only toggles UI.
